answer: activate is a single Operational-mode command whose first parameter selects the function: swimage (activates the currently installable image, implies a system restart; db-action = auto (default) | empty-db | upgrade-db | rollback; label; -f skips confirmation), database (activates the currently inactive database, implies a restart; restart-type cold|warm, default cold; db-instance active/manual/oneday/onehour/oneweek/rollback/temp; db-passphrase 40..200 chars; sanity-check-override false by default), activate-file (file-type, clear-type full|keep-networking|initialize-from-script, default full), location-led (entity = chassis or card, led-mode flash (default) | solid, timeout 0..120 s, default 0 = no timeout, terminate with terminate location-led), loopback (WSS loopback on an nmc-ID), eqpt-fw (resource + fw-image-name), krp, otdr and otdr-fiber-check. For database snapshots there is a separate command: activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override true|false]; its pre-condition is that a snapshot was already taken with take-snapshot, db-instance defaults to temp and sanity-check-override to false.

capabilities is the per-card one: show capabilities-<name>, where name is the name of the card, retrieves that card's capabilities. l0-capabilities is the photonic one: show l0-capabilities takes no parameters and shows the capability details related to the node's Layer 0 functions. oadm-capabilities is the add/drop one: show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], where max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees (20; degrees exist only on OADM node types, and an ILA node is 0 by convention because it has only 2 fixed directions) and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups (110, OADM node types only; 0 means not supported). All three are show-only and available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show controller-card-<name> for just the controller: it returns redundancy-status (active | standby | not-in-service, default not-in-service), redundancy-standby-status (ready-synchronized, not-ready-synchronizing (default), not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out, card-not-present), number-of-switchover-events and time-of-last-switchover (both visible only on the active controller), and additional-details (0..128 chars). For any card in the shelf use card: add/set/show/delete card-<name> with required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, chassis-name, slot-name, subslot-name, power-profile, admin-state (lock/maintenance/unlock, default unlock), oper-state, avail-state, category, last-reboot-reason/time. For what a card model supports use show supported-card-<card-type>: supported-subtype, default-card-mode and supported-card-mode, card-width, category, grid-mode-support, max-power-draw, location-led-support, console-port-support, support-serdes-config, supported-bands, supported-features.

macsec-entity is the Ethernet MACsec one: add/set/show/delete macsec-entity-<name> with supporting-facility (an ethernet facility), enabled (default true), link-security-control must-secure (default) | should-secure, replay-protection enable/disable, replay-protection-window 0..4294967295 (default 0), and the read-only negotiated-cipher-suite. Its cipher terms live in mka-policy (macsec-cipher-suite, confidentiality-offset, sak-rekey-interval 0|30..65535 s, default 30s, key-server-priority), referenced from macsec-mka. secure-entity is the optical/L1 one: add/set/show/delete secure-entity-<name> with supporting-facility (optical-carrier, odu or OTUflex), remote-secure-entity, enabled (default false), re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s (default 28800), re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic | continue-traffic (default continue-traffic) and traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s (default 0). Its cipher terms are read-only in secure-entity-sa-proposal: encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none, dh-group ecp-521.

ase-idler-service is the service-level ASE idler filling function on a card (add/delete/set/show ase-idler-service-<name>): ase-idler-enable enabled|disabled (default disabled) turns ASE filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum, and ase-idler-state reports ase-enabled, ase-partially-enabled, ase-faulted or ase-disabled (default ase-disabled); function is idler. ase-idler-source is the hardware pump that produces the ASE signal (set/show only): pump-enable enabled|disabled (default disabled), pump-state, target-output-power -3.00..20.50 dBm (default 13), plus admin-state, supporting-input-port and supporting-output-port; function is ase-idler-source. sw-service does not belong with them at all: it is a software command, show sw-service-<sv-name> / show sw-services, listing software services and containers on the node with state off|ok|fail, cpu-usage, memory-usage, uptime, last-start-time and reboot-count.

No, they are the destructive ones. change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]enabled|disabled toggles Zero Touch Provisioning; change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot, while change-ztp-mode disabled stops ZTP even if it is already in progress. Check the current setting with show ztp. clear [-f] recover-mode has no parameters and clears the recover-mode flag: it confirms the current configuration as is, re-enables communication with the line cards and may reconfigure traffic settings, so it may be traffic impacting. Both are Operational mode and both take -f to skip the confirmation. The carrier-mode commands are harmless read-only queries: show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> and show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> just display capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status and supported-subtypes.

State: show third-party-app-<app-name> (also show third-party-app-info-<location-id>/<app-name>) gives state = running | stopped | failed (default stopped), enable true|false (default false; if enabled the app is started and restarts with the system), plus version, vendor, product, label and information. Firmware side: show third-party-fw-<fw-name> gives file-status valid|invalid|missing, path, version, crc, vendor, part-number, nsa-upgrade-version (versions from which the upgrade is non service affecting), present-in-eqpt and applicable-eqpt (max 80 elements each). Clearing: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value> clears third party apps. To control rather than clear it, use appctl [app-name=] [command=]restart|netls|exec [target=]<system or chassis/card AID, default system> [parameters=], with up to 50 parameter elements for restart or exec.

Per-session is cli-session-config: set cli-session-config-<session-id> cli-lines <10..1000, default 40> gives you more rows for that login only; it also carries cli-columns 80..4000 (default 80), interactive-mode true/false (set per CLI session and not persistent) and display-timestamp (default false). The protocol as a whole is cli: set/show cli with enabled (default true; you cannot disable CLI from within a CLI session), port 1..65535 (default 22, ssh), script-dir, default-interactive-mode (default true, affects only newly created sessions) and show-alarm-columns (default default-columns, global effect on all sessions). The two system-configuration ones are config (show config [entity-id|entity-type], displays non-default configuration recursively from the current scope; show config | display commands makes a restore script) and extended-config (add/delete/show extended-config-<name>, a non-standard config whose name must match one known by the system and which introduces exceptional behavior globally).

The generic attribute assignment is set: set [-f|-v] [<entity id>] <attribute> <value> [...] [<filter>], operational and candidate mode, at least one attribute-value pair, all pairs on the same managed entity, wildcards (card-*, port-1-4-*), ranges card-1-[1..4] and lists, and it prompts for confirmation when the request may have traffic impact or implicitly affects multiple instances (-f forces, -v validates). set-alarm-state is a separate operation: set-alarm-state [state=]<none|ack|close> [[acknowledge-text=]<0..256 chars>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<1 to 10 alarm ids>); state is mandatory, acknowledge-text optional. set-time is the time one: set-time [new-time=]<ISO 8601, e.g. 2021-02-06T11:16:58Z or +/-hh:mm>, only applicable when time-source is manual (NTP not enabled); read it back with time. The one ending in -set is named-value-set: add/set/delete/show named-value-set-<db-entry-name>/<named-value-set-name> [value <1..1024 chars>].

mc is the Media Channel: add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <MHz> upper-frequency <MHz>; the system derives center-frequency and slot-width, and the supporting card must be part of a Degree (not an ADG). nmc is the Network Media Channel, the actual carrier slot: add nmc-<name> parent-facility (an MC or an OMS) center-frequency (190650000..196700000 MHz) [width 15000..200000 MHz, default 35000, set to the 3 dB signal bandwidth matching the transponder baud rate], plus input/output-attenuation-target (0..15 dB, default max), power-actual-rx/tx and the ASE insertion attributes. The fillers are read-mostly placeholders for unused spectrum: show mc-f-<name> (Media Channel Filler) reports lower-frequency, upper-frequency and slot-width only; nmc-f (Network Media Channel Filler) allows set of admin-state and alarm-report-control and shows alloc-/actual- lower and upper frequency and bandwidth (alloc-bandwidth default 75000 MHz), power-actual-tx/rx and monitoring-state.

The scan is run by activate: activate otdr [entity=]<port> [otdr-file-prefix=] triggers a measurement on the target OTDR port, and activate otdr-fiber-check [entity=]<ots-r-id> triggers a manual OTDR based fiber check (rejected if a manual scan or automatic Raman fiber check is already running; up to 3 tests are executed). You tune it in otdr-ptp: otdr-range auto or 0..300.0 km (set to fiber length plus 10 percent), otdr-pulse-width auto or 10..20000 ns, otdr-measurement-speed fast/medium/slow/precision/auto/high-precision, otdr-ior auto or 1.0..2.0, otdr-fiber-type (auto, SSMF, SMF-ULL, LEAF ...), otdr-resolution auto or 0.4..100.0, otdr-direction-mode (default counter-prop-in-service), peak-power auto or 5..14.5, launching-fiber-length 0..50 m (default 0). The answer comes out of otdr-ptp too: otdr-fiber-break-distance (km, or not-available), otdr-last-measurement and otdr-last-measurement-file (.sor). show otdr-<name> gives live otdr-state (not-available/idle/measuring/finished/fail), otdr-measurement-time, otdr-measurement-port/direction and otdr-error.

For the name server it is the origin attribute on dns-server: add/set/show dns-server-<address> [origin dhcp|manual], default manual. An entry with origin dhcp was assigned by a DHCP server and will be re-learned, so convert it to manual by changing this attribute rather than deleting it. The scope is set globally by dns assignment-method = manual | dhcp | both (default both), together with dns enabled (default true) and dns search (must contain at least one dot; set to an empty string to clear). For the relay there are two levels: dhcp-relay is global, with mode disabled (default) | ipv4 | ipv6 and server-address (at least one IP must be configured when enabled); and if-dhcp-relay-<if-name> dhcp-relay-enabled true|false, default false, enables the relay on that specific interface and obeys the global dhcp-relay settings. A relay does nothing if either the global mode is disabled or the interface flag is still false.

clear [-f] system [type=]<factory-reset | full-wipe | inactive> [[target=]<system, chassis or card AID>] [[restart-behavior=]<restart (default) | shutdown>] does the secure wipe. factory-reset resets the system or a given equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing files and user configurations; it does not take effect for G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E) but is supported on the G30 FRCU controller, and factory-reset with shutdown is not supported on L0 cards. full-wipe cleans the entire system and reinstalls software on the controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, and requires a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover. inactive only clears the inactive software partition. The one that leaves logs and performance data behind is clear [-f] database [clear-type=full (default) | keep-networking | initialize-from-script]: it sets the NE database to default and reboots, and explicitly does not wipe logs, PM data or other non-configuration data.

Read show unprovisioned-inventory-<chassis-serial-number>/<slot-name>: it lists inventory detected but not yet accepted by the Node Controller in a Multi-Chassis configuration, with hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and detection-timestamp (the last time the Node Controller saw it). Cross-check the cabling with show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port>, which reports src-chassis, dst-chassis and src-chassis-state / dst-chassis-state as node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned. On the chassis object, show chassis-<name> gives is-node-controller, chassis-role (unknown | main-chassis | sub-chassis), expected-serial-number (which tells the NC the serial number of a sub-chassis) and equipment-discovery-ready, which stays false until all equipment was discovered at startup. To accept the shelf, add chassis-<name> required-type <G31|G32|G34c|G42> expected-serial-number <serial>.

On the amplifier object, control-mode decides it: auto-max-pw (default, the system sets the gain automatically targeting maximum output power) or manual. In manual mode you set gain-target (0..40 dB, default 0.0) and output-voa-attenuation (0..30 dB); in auto mode you can only bias it with gain-adjustment (-20.00..20.00 dB, default 0, only on function pa or inline). amp-control-support says whether auto-max-pw is even allowed (auto or manual-only), and gain-range-control follows control-mode (manual forces manual, auto-max-pw forces auto), with gain-range-target standard|low|high. What stops output entirely: amplifier-enable is disabled by default and must be set to enabled, and output power also depends on the OSC signal for node-type ILA and on OMS facilities plus an OXcon for node-type OADM; forced-shutdown true shuts a dual-band amplifier down; admin-state lock; and an input OLOS shutdown, soaked by olos-shutdown-soak-timer (0..2000 ms) unless olos-shutdown-disable is true.

Read the member: show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> state, which is active, standby, available or unknown, alongside role = working or protection and transport-entity. At group level, show protection-group-<name> gives pg-state (no-request, forced-to-working, sf-on-working, wait-to-restore, unavailable (default) and so on), last-switch-trigger, remaining-wtr and switch-failure-reason. The settings that govern a switch are on protection-group: switching-mode unidirectional (default) | bidirectional, reversion-mode revertive | non-revertive (default), hold-off-timer 0..10000 ms (default 0), wtr-timer 60..720 s (default 300, revertive only), the triggers client-side-olos-trigger, client-side-sd-trigger, network-side-csf-trigger and network-side-sd-trigger (all disabled by default), pg-request (clear, manual-to-working/protection, forced-to-working/protection, protection-lockout, exercise) and pg-control-request freeze | clear-freeze. Operate it with protection-switch [operation-type=]force|lockout|manual|release [switch-target=] [protection-group=].

Trigger it with verify [-f] fiber-connection [target-select=]<port-id> [allow-switching]: allow-switching false (default) verifies active paths only, true lets the system switch the OPSM so inactive/protection paths are covered too. The pre-condition is that equipment-policies cable-id-control is set to enabled; the command prompts for confirmation unless -f is given, is non-blocking, and raises the CID-verification-in-progress alarm against the NE until all queued requests finish. Watch progress with show cable-id-status: cable-id-state = idle | running-incl-switching | running-no-switching, and test-progress as a string such as N out of M completed. Read the result with show [-r] cable-id-path-<name>: card-type-a/port-a and card-type-z/port-z (CableID is sourced/terminated only by CAD10A and RD20TM), port-a-to-port-z and port-z-to-port-a path-status enabled|disabled, last-test-status not-verified|pass|fail, last-test-qualifier up-to-date|out-dated, last-test-timestamp and additional-info (Cable-ID-MISMATCH means misconnected fiber, timeout means wrong or loose port). show cable-id lists the entities and terminate cable-id stops running tests.

Where authentication is sent is decided by security-policies aaa-authentication-method: local-only (default), local-first-then-remote, remote-first-then-local, or remote-unavailable-then-local. If it is still local-only the node never queries RADIUS. The companion is aaa-authorization-method (local-only default, local-first-then-remote, remote-if-authenticated-else-local, remote-unavailable-then-local); after changing it the user must log out and back in. The server itself is aaa-server-<server-name>: protocol-supported RADIUS (default) or TACACSPLUS, server-address, server-priority 1-10 (order of precedence), server-port default 49, server-port-authentication default 1812, server-port-accounting default 1813, shared-secret (max 64 chars, default sharedkey), source-ip, role-supported authentication/authorization/accounting, enabled true by default. What happens when it does not answer is governed by timeout 1..90 s (default 5) and retry 0..5 (default 3), with timeout x (retry + 1) required to be under 5 minutes, plus the fallback chosen in aaa-authentication-method.

For the automation account use ssh-authorized-key: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label]. Each entry holds a trusted public key for SSHv2 user authentication, the user may be local or remote, key-id is a unique name, public-key is up to 2048 characters in OpenSSH/PEM form, and public-key-algorithm is shown as ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521 or ssh-rsa2048/3072/4096. Enable it with security-policies ssh-authentication-method = public-key or public-key-or-password (default password). For trusting a remote host the node copies files to, use ssh-known-host: add ssh-known-host-<id> address <hostname/IPv4/IPv6> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value>, with ssh-ed25519 also allowed from R9.0; how strictly it is enforced is set by security-policies ssh-strict-host-key-checking = strict or relaxed (default relaxed). The node's own identity is ssh-host-key (show only, one per algorithm, auto-generated in the default DB, additional keys added or overwritten via ssh-keygen), showing public-key, fingerprint-algorithm md5|sha256 and fingerprint.

The key agreement policy lives in mka-policy: add/set/show/delete mka-policy-<name> with key-server-priority (used by MKA to select the key server), macsec-cipher-suite (cipher suites for Secure Association Key derivation), confidentiality-offset (number of octets in a frame sent unencrypted) and sak-rekey-interval. The session key rollover is that sak-rekey-interval, the Secure Association Key rekey interval in seconds, range 0|30..65535, default 30s. The policy is bound to the port through macsec-mka: set macsec-mka-<name> mka-policy <name>, plus connectivity-association-key and connectivity-association-key-name (0..64 chars), psk-lifetime/psk-expiration-warning (1..173 days, default 14), psk-lifetime-enable and the read-only is-key-server and psk-configured-timestamp. Watch the channels with show sc-tx-<name>/<index> and show sc-rx-<name>/<index>: sci-tx/sci-rx (16-character hex Secure Channel Identifier), state in-use | not-in-use, association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number. The port-level container is macsec-entity, bound to the ethernet facility.

netconf: set/show netconf, enabled true by default (you cannot disable NETCONF from within a NETCONF session), port default 830 over ssh (range 1..65535), hello-timeout 1..3600 s default 2, annotate-cli-name false, static-info-in-notifs up to 10 YANG identifiers. grpc (gNMI/gRPC): set/show grpc, enabled true by default, port default 50051, gnmi-get-encoding-granularity per-path or per-object (default per-object). restconf: enabled true by default, but the transports differ, https-enabled true with https-port 8181, while http-enabled is false by default (and RESTCONF HTTP is not supported in secure mode) with http-port 8080; cookie-timeout 1..300 minutes, default 5. So nothing on that list is off out of the box except RESTCONF over plain HTTP. For reference the CLI itself is set/show cli, enabled true, port 22. All are Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] is Operational mode and asks for confirmation unless -f is given. If you omit resource-id it restarts the active node controller, and if you omit type it does a warm restart by default. warm reboots the processor of a CHM6, UCM4 and similar cards and is non service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes; for XMM4 a warm reboot is non-service-affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, again with connectivity back within five minutes, except that a cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting although visibility is lost, while cold reboot of CHM6 or UCM4 is service affecting. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. No, you cannot assume every card behaves alike: not all cards support all restart types. Cards accept cold, warm and shutdown; a card sub-component accepts cold and warm (list them with show card resources); a tom accepts cold only.

Three things must be in place. First the global switch: set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates <enabled|disabled>, which is disabled by default; on enabling, existing TOMs are not retro-configured, templates only apply from that moment onward, and on disabling existing serdes configuration is kept. Second a template keyed to the part number: add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <1..16 chars>] [card-types-applicable] [ports-applicable], where ports-applicable defaults to all ports (or a list of up to 20 port names such as T1, T10). Third the values: add serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<entry-name> value <value>, one entry per serdes parameter, for example RxAmplitude, RxEQ, TxEQ, TxEQAdaptive, RxPreCursor, RxPostCursor. The card must also support it, show supported-card-<card-type> support-serdes-config must be true. Then when a TOM with that part-number is plugged in the template is applied automatically; manual serdes settings are kept even if they deviate, swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets serdes and re-applies the new template, and apply-template forces re-application.

ots (Optical Transport Section) represents the fiber span itself: fiber-type-tx/rx (default SSMF), fiber-length-tx/rx auto or 0..500.0 km, span-loss-transmit/receive 0..80 dB, span-loss-derived-rx/tx measured from OSC, span-loss-reference configured|measured (default measured), external-attenuation-tx/rx 0..30 dB, target-power-setting manual|auto|auto-plan (default auto) and laser-safety-mode OPLM or APSD. oms (Optical Multiplex Section) is the multiplexed band on a degree: grid-mode flexible (default) or fixed-50G-96ch / fixed-75G-64ch / fixed-100G-48ch / fixed-150G-40ch, monitoring-mode, attenuation-control-mode-rx/tx auto by default, lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz, band-allowed/actual/target, assigned-degree. ops (Optical Physical Section) is the per-port physical section: role tributary, multi-carrier, general-purpose (default), ase-input or active-multi-carrier, input-psd-profile -30..-6 dBm/12.5GHz (default -6), port-expansion no|y-cable. osc (Optical Supervisory Channel) carries the supervisory traffic: osc-mode OC3 (155 Mbit/s) or 1GE for HSC OLS, osc-control auto|manual (default auto), target-output-power -2.5..4.5 dBm, voa-attenuation-target-rx 0..30 dB (default 10), l0-comm-interface-type ipv4 or ipv6.

The behaviour is configured on the tributary client termination, trib-ptp, with tributary-disable-action: it says what the NE does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed, either shutting off the laser or inserting a replacement signal. Values are laser-shut-off (the default), none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais and send-nos (G30 only). So by default the node turns the client-facing laser off. Delay it with tributary-disable-holdoff-timer, 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff disabled; it is only applicable when the TDA action is laser-turnoff, holding the optical signal until the timer expires. Related switches on the same object are near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode (BERSD-ODU triggers ALS, default disabled) and forward-defect-trigger (true by default: an incoming client forward defect such as LF or ODU-AIS flows through to the line side, otherwise it triggers an egress TDA action). Set it with, for example, set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.
